transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… mainly, I’m here because I feel like I can’t keep my work in order anymore. I work with laundry and dry cleaning, and there are all these tickets, receipts, notes from the work area, customer jobs coming in and going out, and it all just seems to end up piled together. I’ll think I’m keeping track of it, but then I look down and I don’t know what’s what or what needs to be handled first.

It’s embarrassing, honestly, because this is the kind of thing I feel like I should be able to manage. But lately it’s like I’m constantly sorting through scraps of paper and trying to remember which customer is waiting on what, and the more I try to straighten it out, the more mixed up it feels. That’s what made me think I should talk to someone, because it’s starting to feel like I can’t stay on top of it the way I need to.
Have you had this kind of trouble staying organized for as long as you can remember, even back when you were a child?

Yes… yes, honestly, when I think back, it was there even in grade school. I wasn’t a kid who was failing or anything like that — that was part of what made it confusing, I think. Teachers would tell my mother that I was bright, that I could understand the work, but then they’d always add something like, “She’s scattered,” or “She needs to settle down,” or “She has to stop talking out of turn.”

I remember losing papers all the time — homework sheets, permission slips, things I was supposed to bring home or bring back. My desk would get messy, and I’d have things stuffed in folders or loose in my bag. And I needed reminders to finish my work, because I’d start something and then somehow drift off or get pulled into talking or doing something else. So, yes, it wasn’t just recent. It’s kind of been a pattern for as long as I can remember, even if I didn’t really have a name for it back then.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention on tasks, even when you want to focus?

Yes, I do. That’s actually one of the things that frustrates me the most, because I’ll sit down and think, “Okay, I’m going to go through these orders carefully,” especially at work with the dry-cleaning tickets and what has to be checked in or matched up. And at the start I really am trying. I’m not just ignoring it.

But then after a few minutes, my mind is somewhere else. I’ll suddenly be thinking about the labels on the clothes, or something I need to remember for choir, or some little thing at home, and then I come back to what’s in front of me and realize I don’t actually know what I just looked at. Like I may have gone down half a stack of orders, but I can’t trust that I really checked them properly, so I have to start over or go back through them again.

It’s not that I don’t care. I do care, which almost makes it worse. I want to focus, and I’ll even tell myself to focus, but it’s like my attention slips off before I notice it happening.
Do these same problems with attention and organization also cause trouble for you at home?

Yes… it does. At home it shows up, but honestly the bigger problems outside of work are more with church things I used to help organize. I sing in the choir and I used to help more with planning — like keeping track of who was doing what, what needed to be brought, little schedules and lists and messages — and I’ve had to step back from some of that because people were getting frustrated with me.

And I don’t blame them, really. I’d mean to follow up with someone, or I’d have a note somewhere about what we decided, and then I couldn’t find it or I’d mix it up with something else. Then somebody would say, “I thought you were handling that,” and I’d feel awful because I really was trying to handle it. It wasn’t that I didn’t care.

At the shop it’s caused real trouble too — late orders, billing getting confused, tense moments with staff and customers when something wasn’t ready or the charge didn’t match what someone expected. Those are the times I feel the worst, because it affects other people, not just me being messy or forgetful by myself.
Do you often act or speak before thinking?

Yes, I do. I don’t always realize I’m doing it until after, but I’ll jump in before the person has even finished asking me something.

It happens with my daughter a lot. She’ll be trying to explain what she needs or ask me about something, and I’ll think I know where she’s going with it, so I answer too soon. Then she’ll say, “Mom, that’s not what I was asking,” and I feel embarrassed because I didn’t even let her finish.

It happens at work too, with customers. Someone starts asking about an order or a price or when something will be ready, and I’ll answer based on what I think they mean, but then it turns out they were asking a different question. Same thing when someone is training me or explaining a new way to do something — I’ll jump in with “Oh, okay, I know,” and then I find out I missed the important part because I talked too soon. I don’t mean to be rude. It’s more like the answer is already coming out of my mouth before I’ve really waited and listened all the way through.
Do you have unwanted thoughts that keep coming into your mind and feel hard to dismiss?

I’m not sure I’d describe it that way, no. I mean, I do get thoughts stuck in my head sometimes, like anyone does, especially if I’m worried I forgot something or if something went badly and I keep replaying it. But I don’t know that I have unwanted thoughts that just keep forcing their way in and I can’t dismiss them.

Usually it’s more like my mind wanders or jumps around, or I remember something at the wrong time, but not like a particular scary or disturbing thought repeating over and over. If you mean something more specific by unwanted thoughts, I might need you to explain it a little, because I don’t think that’s one of the main things I’ve noticed.
Have you been feeling down or depressed معظم الأيام lately?

I don’t know that I’d say depressed most days, no. I mean, I have days where I feel worn down or discouraged, especially when I’ve messed something up or I feel like I’ve disappointed somebody, but I don’t think it’s like a steady sadness every day.

Lately I’ve been frustrated with myself more than anything. Sometimes I’ll get quiet or feel kind of heavy for a bit, but it usually feels connected to whatever happened, not like I wake up every day feeling depressed. So… I guess my answer would be no, not most days, at least not how I understand “depressed.”
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

I don’t think so, not in the sense of worrying all the time about lots of different things when nothing is actually happening. I do worry about things when there’s something in front of me, like if I’m not sure I handled something right or if I’m trying to remember what I was supposed to do, but I wouldn’t say I sit around worrying about everything for no reason.

Sometimes my mind keeps circling around something practical, like, “Did I forget to take care of that?” or “Was I supposed to call someone back?” But that feels more like I’m trying to keep track of things, not like I’m just anxious about the future all day. I don’t know if that makes sense.

So I guess my answer is… not really. I get concerned about things, sure, but I haven’t noticed constant worrying about a bunch of different things when there isn’t an immediate problem.
